cohort: 180 antenatal patients at 37 completed weeks of gestation with no high-risk factors
finding: Non-stress tests are a reliable screening tool for detecting high-risk fetuses in low-risk mothers, with abnormal tests associated with increased probability of adverse outcomes such as meconium-stained liquor, low APGAR score, and NICU admission.
mod_finding: Abnormal non-stress tests were associated with a lower percentage of normal delivery (23.91% vs 60.4%) and a higher percentage of cesarean section (63.04% vs 33.58%), with fetal distress being the most common indication for cesarean section in the abnormal group (68.96%).
